summary: Repository-mining causal study of 151 open-source Java projects (74 with detectable agentic-AI adoption via CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.cursorrules/copilot-instructions/Aider config or Co-Authored-By trailers, 77 propensity-matched controls) over 1,811 monthly Arcan snapshots, using staggered difference-in-differences (Borusyak imputation). Architectural smell density falls 6.7%, but raw smell counts are flat (+1.1%, p=0.82) while LOC grows 12.8%, so the drop is a denominator effect, not an architectural improvement.

claims.claim: Adoption lowers architectural smell density by 6.7%
claims.evidence: Table 1: Borusyak ATT -0.0698 (SE 0.0239, 95% CI [-0.117,-0.023], p=0.004); Sun-Abraham -6.6% (p=0.005); 1,811 obs., 151 repos, repo and time FE, clustered SEs.

claims.claim: The density decline is a denominator effect: smell counts unchanged, code grows
claims.evidence: §4.5, Fig. 4: raw smell counts +1.1% (p=0.82), LOC +12.8% (p=0.003), package count +9.7% (p=0.032); per-type counts CD/HL/GC all p>0.25.
§4.4, Fig. 3: pre-period event-study Wald chi2=1.64, df=5, p=0.896; authors note this cannot exclude smooth pre-trends absorbed by FE (§6).

claims.claim: Result is robust to attrition and stale observations
claims.evidence: §6: Lee bounds [-9.9%, -2.3%] but upper bound's CI includes zero (p=0.239), i.e. under worst-case attrition the effect is indistinguishable from null; aggressive stale-observation filtering (N=94) makes it non-significant. Authors disclose both.

claims.claim: Unstable dependencies may be rising in raw count
claims.evidence: UD raw count +5.8% (raw p=0.032, Holm-adjusted p=0.128); explicitly labelled suggestive.

patterns.note: Uses presence of CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.cursorrules/copilot-instructions as the adoption marker; no evidence about the files' effect per se.
Architectural smell detection (Arcan) used as the outcome; shows density metrics can mislead when the treatment changes code size.
Field evidence from real OSS repositories with a causal design: short-term agentic adoption does not measurably increase architectural smells in mature Java systems.

methodology.sample: 151 Java OSS repos (74 treated, 77 controls) from 90+90 matched; 1,811 monthly snapshots over 13-month windows; 29 repos lost (16 treated, 13 control)
methodology.baselines: Propensity-matched never-treated controls; Borusyak imputation and Sun-Abraham TWFE estimators
methodology.models: n/a (tool adoption: Claude Code 44, Copilot 14, Cursor 15, Codex 1 retained)
methodology.variance: Clustered SEs, 95% CIs, wild cluster bootstrap, Lee bounds, Holm correction across smell types
methodology.ablations: Per-type, per-tool (exploratory), stale-observation sensitivity, covariate adjustment, Bacon decomposition, autocomplete-contamination sensitivity
methodology.contamination_controls: Content validation of ambiguous markers (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md); attenuation-bias correction for undetected AI use in controls (c=8.9%)

standards.peer_review: Accepted at SEAA 2026 (Springer LNCS), author's accepted manuscript
standards.artifacts: Replication package with curated 151-repo monthly panel at github.com/Oliver1703dk/seaa2026-replication-package

biases.detail: Differential attrition (17.8% treated vs 14.4% control), concentrated among the largest projects lost to Arcan JVM memory limits; worst-case Lee bound includes null.
Adoption proxied by config files/trailers; inline autocomplete undetectable, and AGENTS.md is mapped to Codex though it is used by several hosts. Intensity of use is unknown.
Effect still growing at h=6 months; long-run architectural impact unobserved.

coi.affiliations: SDU Software Engineering, University of Southern Denmark
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: None evaluated favorably; tool adoption studied observationally
coi.detail: Academic authors; no vendor ties disclosed or apparent.

verdict_reason: Careful, peer-reviewed causal design with multiple estimators, pre-trend tests, multiplicity correction, transparent threats (including that worst-case attrition reaches null) and a full replication package. Main contribution, that density metrics mislead when AI changes code volume, is well supported. Limited to short-horizon effects in mature Java OSS.
applicability: Directly relevant to a Java backend team: in mature Java codebases, short-term agentic adoption grew code ~13% without measurably increasing architectural smell counts, so the main risk is code volume growth rather than immediate architectural decay. Practical takeaways for the several repositories: track raw smell/dependency counts and LOC separately (not only density) in Sonar/Arcan-style dashboards, watch unstable-dependency counts, and monitor beyond six months. It does not address cross-repo contracts, spec-driven workflows, or which agent host is used beyond the exploratory, under-powered per-tool split.

conflicts_with.detail: That multivocal review reports LLM-assisted coding often amplifies design debt; this causal study finds no increase in architectural smell counts in the short term for mature Java repos.
